chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man performed Tawaf by the Kaaba, then went out and performed Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwah. While he was performing Tawaf, he remembered that he had left out one circuit of his Tawaf by the House. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should return to the House and complete his Tawaf, then return to As-Safa and Al-Marwah and complete what remains.' I said: 'What if he started with As-Safa and Al-Marwah before starting with the House?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should go to the House, perform Tawaf by it, then resume his Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwah.' I said: 'So what is the difference between these two?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Because this one had entered into something of the Tawaf, and this one had not entered into anything of it.'

key_terms.صَفَا وَالْمَرْوَة: Safa and Marwah, the two hills between which pilgrims walk during Sa'i
key_terms.طَوَاف: Tawaf, the ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if they realize they forgot a circuit of Tawaf while performing Sa'i?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the structural integrity of Hajj rituals by distinguishing between a mere sequence error and a substantive omission based on whether the pilgrim had already entered the state of Tawaf. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that if one begins Sa'i before Tawaf, the Tawaf is considered incomplete and must be performed first, whereas if Tawaf was started first, the Sa'i is merely delayed and can be completed after the Tawaf is finished. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the sequential dependency of these pillars, ensuring the ritual's validity through precise adherence to the order prescribed by the Prophet and the Imams.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A man performs Tawaaf by the Kaaba, then he goes out, so he performs Tawaaf between Al-Safa and Al-Marwan. So, while he is in the midst of his Tawaaf, he remembers that he had neglected a circuit by the Kaaba. Heasws said: ‘He should return to the House (Kaaba), and he should complete his Tawaaf, then he should return to Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, and he should complete whatever remains’. I said, ‘Supposing he begins with Al-Safa and Al-Marwan before he begins with the House (Kaaba)?’ So heasws said: ‘He should go to the House (Kaaba), so he would perform Tawaaf by it, then he would resume his Tawaaf between Al-Safa and Al-Marwan’. I said, ‘So what is the difference between these two?’ Heasws said: ‘Because this one had entered into something from the Tawaaf, and this one did not enter into anything from it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who performs Tawaf around al-Ka‘bah, then goes to al-Safa’ and al-Marwah to perform Tawaf, and remembers that he has left out certain parts of Tawaf around the House. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must go back to the House to complete his Tawaf, then come to al-Safa’ and al-Marwah to complete the remaining parts.’ I then asked, ‘What happens if one begins with al-Safa’ and al-Marwah before the House?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He must go to the House for Tawaf, then perform Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah again.’ I asked, ‘What is the difference between the two?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘This has done certain parts of Tawaf and this one has not done anything.’”
